scope: 39 local Rust timezone, calendar registry and zoned relative dependencies. Implementation and requirement statuses unchanged.
source_comparison: Frozen Temporal proposal via durable checklist rows. ECMA-262 remains requested authority.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.10 step 4: Build the arithmetic-only registry for calendar resolution.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The arithmetic registry leaves the three optional table slots empty. Its resolve method can still supply the arithmetic providers.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.10 step 4: Register one validated table per supported table ID.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The registry assigns already validated tables to the Chinese, Dangi, or Islamic Umm al-Qura slots and rejects a repeated slot. The table constructor owns chronology validation.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.10 step 4: Resolve aliases and available providers for a typed calendar ID.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Resolves two documented aliases and ASCII-insensitive names through arithmetic and table registries. Known uninstalled tables remain distinguishable from invalid identifiers.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.10 step 4: Enumerate the providers available for calendar resolution.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The private runtime provider inventory consists of the supported arithmetic calendars and supplied optional tables. This iterator supplies that registry view.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.36 steps 2.a–2.c and §12.3.10 step 4: Resolve the parsed calendar annotation or ISO default.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The caller supplies a parsed Temporal string shape. Calendar annotation selects the registry key and an absent annotation picks iso8601. String grammar and coercion belong to the caller.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.26 step 2: Validate the compiled table providers before calendar projection.
reviewed_rows.evidence: With compiled_calendars, typed constructors validate the shipped Chinese, Dangi and Umm al-Qura tables before registry assembly. Their subsequent projection is owned by TableCalendar.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Compute the monthly weekday used by a named-zone footer.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Gregorian weekday arithmetic finds the requested occurrence. A fifth occurrence that falls after month end selects the preceding occurrence, implementing the last-week form.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Check the footer rule fields used for named-zone offsets.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checks month/week/weekday, day/Julian index and signed transition-time bounds before footer rule evaluation. The checks validate the local shape only.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Convert a footer rule into local transition seconds.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Monthly, zero-based day and Julian rules select a Gregorian day. Julian rules skip leap day. The supplied transition seconds are added to the local day.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Validate standard and daylight offsets before footer evaluation.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The constructor bounds offsets below one day in magnitude and validates both optional switch rules. The generated evidence supplies the distinct recurrence assumptions for shipped data.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Convert footer switches to UTC using the prior offsets.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The daylight start subtracts the standard offset from its local switch. The end subtracts the daylight offset. The pair is absent for a fixed footer.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.3.46 steps 9.a and 10.b: Check whether a footer event changes the offset.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rejects equal-offset daylight and standard states. Checks the offset immediately before and at an event, with explicit handling for a year-boundary shortcut and neighboring-year events.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Select the offset in the applicable footer year.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Compares epoch seconds with the two UTC events. The daylight interval is half-open and wraps across the year for southern rules. The caller selects the applicable year.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Resolve the latest footer switch across neighboring years.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checks events in year minus one through year plus one and records the most recent switch at or before the input. Tied event ordering follows the local start/end predicates.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Select named-zone footer offset for epoch seconds.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Fixed rules return the standard offset. Month-shaped daylight rules can use the guarded window shortcut, with year or neighboring-year comparison for remaining inputs. Mapping is local to the generated provider premises.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Validate offsets and ordered events for named-zone lookup.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Initial and transition offsets must lie strictly within one day. Explicit events must be strictly increasing and in Instant range. A supplied FutureRule already has typed construction checks.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Mark the final explicit event before footer lookup.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Returns the final explicit event in epoch seconds or i64::MIN. Offset lookup compares the floored epoch second to this cutoff before using the supplied footer.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Look up a named-zone offset with exact instant boundaries.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Floors exact Instant nanoseconds to a whole epoch second with integer arithmetic. Looks up the last explicit offset at or before that second, or uses the footer strictly after the cutoff. Returns exact offset nanoseconds.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.13 step 3.a: Supply the full offset list for named-zone candidate checks.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Delegates to the explicit and footer offset visitor. Caller checks candidate round trips, range and ordering separately.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.13 step 3.a: Supply offsets near the requested local timestamp.
reviewed_rows.evidence: A sub-day offset bounds potential candidate seconds to the local second plus or minus 86400. Visits baseline and in-window explicit offsets and relevant footer offsets. Empty clipped windows use the full list. Endpoint straddle premises remain separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.3.46 steps 9.a and 10.b: Search strict next or previous offset changes.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Searches exact explicit and generated recurrence events in the requested direction and skips no-op events. The mapping concerns the installed native data contract, with recurrence and endpoint premises scoped by existing proof.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.13 step 3.a: Visit possible initial, explicit and footer offsets.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Converts offsets to nanoseconds and forwards each encountered value, suppressing repeats while values fit the fixed cache. Candidate validity and any remaining duplicate candidates are checked by the consumer.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.1 steps 1.a and 2: Look up spelling and primary ID by ASCII-insensitive name.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Uses ASCII-folded byte order in the generated sorted records, returns record spelling and independent primary or None for absence.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.8 steps 7–9: Bind a recognized name to the supplied provider.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Looks up the named record and rejects absence. The wrapper requires the injected provider to describe that named zone.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.8 step 9: Return the stored identifier spelling.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Returns the Identifier spelling from the stored named-zone record, preserving an alias spelling when applicable.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.15 step 2.e: Read the primary ID used for named-zone comparison.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Exposes the PrimaryIdentifier stored separately from Identifier in the named-zone record.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.15 steps 2.e and 4: Compare named zones by primary ID.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Compares the primary strings of two already resolved named zones, independent of the attached provider representations. Fixed-offset comparison belongs elsewhere.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: Delegate exact named-zone offset lookup.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards the typed Instant unchanged to the provider bound to the resolved name.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.13 step 3.a: Delegate full offset enumeration for candidate checks.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards the visitor unchanged to the named zone provider. Candidate evaluation and deduplication belong to the consumer.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.13 step 3.a: Delegate local offset enumeration for candidate checks.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards the exact local nanoseconds and visitor unchanged to the named zone provider.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.3.46 steps 9.a and 10.b: Delegate named-zone transition lookup.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards the exact Instant and requested transition direction unchanged to the named zone provider.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone + PartialEq, C: CalendarProvider> ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::until

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.3.37 step 3: Dispatch typed until to zoned difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards typed arguments to the shared date/time difference with the until flag. Public receiver and options evaluation are separate.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone + PartialEq, C: CalendarProvider> ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::since

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.3.38 step 3: Dispatch typed since to zoned difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards typed arguments to the shared date/time difference with the since flag. Public receiver and options evaluation are separate.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone + PartialEq, C: CalendarProvider> ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::difference

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.5.9 steps 2, 7–9: Check typed calendar and date-unit zone equality, then take the difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rejects different calendar IDs, validates typed settings, checks provider equality only for date units, then returns zero or delegates exact target nanoseconds to the shared difference. Generic provider PartialEq is a caller premise.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone, C: CalendarProvider> RelativeAnchor for ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::calendar

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.5.6 step 14: Supply the provider used for calendar date difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Returns the already selected calendar provider. Its date_until operation owns calendar difference.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone, C: CalendarProvider> RelativeAnchor for ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::origin

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.5.7 steps 2 and 5: Supply the anchor instant in exact nanoseconds.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Supplies the exact start epoch nanoseconds for the relative arithmetic and rounding calls.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone, C: CalendarProvider> RelativeAnchor for ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::date_at

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.5.6 steps 2–4: Project an exact instant to its local ISO day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Validates and projects an Instant with the same zone provider, then extracts the ISO epoch day used by the shared date comparison.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone, C: CalendarProvider> RelativeAnchor for ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::endpoint

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.5.5 steps 3, 6 and 7: Supply exact constrained zoned endpoints for relative arithmetic.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Validates typed duration fields and delegates constrained zoned addition. Returns the resulting exact Instant, leaving date, compatible resolution and time addition to checked_add.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone, C: CalendarProvider> RelativeAnchor for ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::clock_at

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.5.6 step 8: Project the local clock for time difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Validates and projects an Instant in the same zone provider and extracts exact time-of-day nanoseconds. The consumer computes the clock difference.

validation.result: 12 Bazel targets passed in the same validation batch.
